issues.item: Catastrophising Others: I worry obsessively about bad things happening to people I care about
issues.explanation: 'Catastrophising Others' is hard to integrate with the rest of the profile and the trauma type. The other items center on childhood physical abuse, mistrust, touch-sensitivity, fragmented memory, guilt, and self-damage; obsessive worry about harm befalling loved ones points to a different threat theme and is not supported by the appraisals or memory content.

issues.item: Door and Lock Checking: I repeatedly check that doors and windows are locked
issues.explanation: 'Door and Lock Checking' suggests a home-intrusion/security threat theme. In this profile, threat is otherwise expressed as interpersonal danger cues (unexpected touch, ominous silence) linked to caregiver abuse. Without matching appraisals or memory content about break-ins or external intruders, this item is difficult to reconcile with the rest of the selected items.

vignette: John, a 55-year-old North American male and fashion designer, has been struggling with a complex interplay of symptoms stemming from childhood physical abuse by his caregiver. His current state is marked by a pervasive sense of vulnerability and mistrust, as well as a deep-seated fear that he will never recover from the trauma he experienced. Growing up in a small Midwestern town, John endured years of brutal beatings at the hands of his father. The abuse was not only physical but also psychological, leaving him with a fragmented memory of the events and an overwhelming sense of guilt. Even now, decades later, John cannot piece together a coherent narrative of what happened to him. When he does recall specific instances of abuse, he feels as if they occurred to someone else-emotionless and detached from his own experience. The trauma has left deep scars on John's psyche. He often ruminates about the actions of others that have wronged him, particularly focusing on how he was victimized by his father. This rumination is accompanied by a relentless self-blame where he questions what he could have done differently to prevent the abuse. These thoughts are compounded by intense nightmares that occur at specific times of day or in certain situations, making it difficult for John to sleep without fear. John's heightened state of alertness is evident in his daily life. He reacts with alarm when someone touches him unexpectedly, a reaction rooted in the unpredictable nature of the beatings he experienced as a child. The absence of sound in his home environment can also trigger a sense of impending danger, making it challenging for John to relax even within the safety of his own house. John's occupation as a fashion designer has not been spared by these symptoms. His constant state of alertness often makes it difficult for him to collaborate effectively with colleagues who frequently touch or pat him on the back in a show of camaraderie, actions that trigger his fight-or-flight response. This hyper-vigilance has led to strained relationships at work and a perception among his peers that he is aloof or disengaged. Over time, John's avoidance behaviors have taken a toll on his personal life as well. His fear of being touched by others has made it difficult for him to maintain close relationships, further isolating him from potential sources of support. The mistrust he harbors towards people stems from the belief that no one can be truly relied upon-a sentiment deeply ingrained by his childhood experiences. John's self-doubt is profound; he believes he will never fully recover from the trauma and fears that his current reactions mean he is "going crazy." These negative appraisals have created a vicious cycle where John feels permanently damaged, unable to escape the shadow of his past. His inability to form a coherent narrative about what happened has only reinforced this belief. Despite his efforts to cope with these overwhelming feelings, John's quality of life has significantly deteriorated. The cumulative impact of his symptoms led him to finally seek help when he realized that his work and personal relationships were being severely affected. He is most afraid of the possibility of never regaining a sense of normalcy or stability. However, amidst this struggle, John also holds hope for a better future. He is eager to explore ways in which he can process his trauma more effectively and regain control over his life. His journey towards healing will involve understanding and making sense of his fragmented memories, addressing his intense feelings of guilt and mistrust, and finding healthier coping mechanisms that do not isolate him further from the world around him. John's story is one of resilience in the face of profound adversity. Through therapy, he hopes to uncover a more coherent narrative of his past, regain trust in others, and ultimately reclaim a sense of control over his life.
